es: Contar una anécdota de un día caótico con modismos bien integrados, cerrarla con una valoración en retrospectiva y explicar dos de ellos con palabras sencillas a alguien que no los conoce.

vocabulary.en: to cut a long story short

teaching.en: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday, which started badly and, as luck would have it, got worse before lunch.
teaching.es: Déjame contarte una anécdota sobre mi lunes caótico, que empezó mal y, quiso la suerte, empeoró antes del almuerzo.
teaching.explanationEs: Anecdote = anécdota; la fórmula Let me tell you… abre la historia. As luck would have it introduce un giro inesperado.
segments: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday, which started
badly and, as luck would have it, got worse before lunch.
teaching.audioText: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday, which started badly and, as luck would have it, got worse before lunch.

teaching.en: My chaotic morning began to go from bad to worse: first my bus broke down, and then my phone died, which was the last straw.
teaching.es: Mi caótica mañana empezó a ir de mal en peor: primero se averió mi autobús y luego se quedó sin batería mi teléfono, y eso fue la gota que colmó el vaso.
teaching.explanationEs: The last straw = lo último que hace que ya no puedas más. Go from bad to worse: la situación empeora paso a paso.
segments: My chaotic morning began to go from bad to worse: first my bus
broke down, and then my phone died, which was the last straw.
teaching.audioText: My chaotic morning began to go from bad to worse: first my bus broke down, and then my phone died, which was the last straw.

teaching.en: Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so the terrible morning turned out to be a blessing in disguise after all.
teaching.es: Por suerte, la reunión se canceló, así que la terrible mañana resultó ser, después de todo, un mal que vino bien.
teaching.explanationEs: A blessing in disguise = algo malo que resulta ser bueno. Luckily marca un giro afortunado.
segments: Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so the terrible morning turned
out to be a blessing in disguise after all.
teaching.audioText: Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so the terrible morning turned out to be a blessing in disguise after all.

teaching.en: We ran to the station and, luckily, we arrived in the nick of time, just as the doors of the train were closing.
teaching.es: Corrimos a la estación y, por suerte, llegamos justo a tiempo, cuando las puertas del tren se estaban cerrando.
teaching.explanationEs: In the nick of time = en el último momento, justo antes de que fuera tarde; es fijo y sin the delante de time.
segments: We ran to the station and, luckily, we arrived in the nick
of time, just as the doors of the train were closing.
teaching.audioText: We ran to the station and, luckily, we arrived in the nick of time, just as the doors of the train were closing.

teaching.en: Dad hit the roof, which means that he was furious; in other words, he shouted, and luckily the neighbours did not hear him.
teaching.es: Papá se puso furioso, lo que significa que estaba muy enfadado; dicho de otra manera, gritó, y por suerte los vecinos no lo oyeron.
teaching.explanationEs: Which means + explicación y in other words + reformulación aclaran un modismo a quien no lo conoce.
segments: Dad hit the roof, which means that he was furious; in other
words, he shouted, and luckily the neighbours did not hear him.
teaching.audioText: Dad hit the roof, which means that he was furious; in other words, he shouted, and luckily the neighbours did not hear him.

teaching.en: In hindsight, the whole chaotic day is a funny anecdote, and to cut a long story short, nobody was hurt and we all laughed.
teaching.es: Con la perspectiva del tiempo, todo aquel día caótico es una anécdota divertida y, para resumir, nadie salió herido y nos reímos todos.
teaching.explanationEs: In hindsight valora el pasado desde el presente; to cut a long story short resume el final sin entrar en detalles.
segments: In hindsight, the whole chaotic day is a funny anecdote, and to
cut a long story short, nobody was hurt and we all laughed.

prompt.es: ¿Qué glosa explica mejor «the last straw» a alguien que no lo conoce?

choices.text: It means I could not take one more problem.
It means I finally found a straw for my drink.
It means the bus was the last one of the day.

feedback.es: La glosa correcta traduce la idea de no poder soportar un problema más; las otras dos leen la expresión de forma literal.

hint.es: Piensa en tres problemas seguidos: ¿qué sentido figurado tiene el último?

origin.text: My phone died, my bus broke down and then the rain started. That was the last straw.

prompt.es: Completa: «Llegamos a la estación justo a tiempo.»

feedback.es: In the nick of time es un modismo fijo y sin artículo: no se añade the.

hint.es: El modismo no lleva the delante de esta palabra.

origin.text: We reached the station in the nick of ___, because the train was already closing its doors and the guard was waving his flag.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Fue la gota que colmó el vaso, lo que significa que ya no podía más.»

answer.text: It was the last straw, which means I could not continue

feedback.es: Después del modismo se añade una coma y which means + explicación sencilla.

hint.es: Empieza con It was the last straw y termina con could not continue.

prompt.es: Lee y elige la glosa sencilla de «in the nick of time».

choices.text: We caught it after a long wait.
We caught it just before it left.
We caught it, although it was already late.

feedback.es: In the nick of time = en el último momento; las puertas se cierran detrás de ellos y el tren arranca enseguida.

origin.text: We ran across the platform and caught the train in the nick of time. The doors closed behind us, and the train began to move before we had even found our seats.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota y elige cómo valora ahora la hablante aquel lunes.

choices.text: As a wasted day that she would like to forget.
As an easy day because nothing important happened.
As a bad day that improved her relationship with her boss.

feedback.es: Con la perspectiva del tiempo lo llama «a blessing in disguise»: un mal día que le permitió hablar abiertamente con su jefe.

origin.audio: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday. My alarm did not ring, so I woke up late, and then my bus broke down. That was the last straw, which means I could not take any more, so I decided to walk. Halfway there I met my boss, who was also walking because his car had broken down. As luck would have it, the meeting was cancelled, so we laughed, had coffee together and called it a day. In hindsight, it was a blessing in disguise, because I had never spoken to him so openly.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige con qué fin añade «which means I could not take any more».

choices.text: To explain an idiom for a listener who may not know it.
To show that she was angry with her boss.
To tell the listener that she missed the bus.

feedback.es: Which means + explicación sencilla es la glosa que aclara «the last straw» a un oyente que quizá no conozca la expresión.

origin.audio: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday. My alarm did not ring, so I woke up late, and then my bus broke down. That was the last straw, which means I could not take any more, so I decided to walk. Halfway there I met my boss, who was also walking because his car had broken down. As luck would have it, the meeting was cancelled, so we laughed, had coffee together and called it a day. In hindsight, it was a blessing in disguise, because I had never spoken to him so openly.

prompt.es: Completa: «Resultó ser un mal que vino bien, porque me hizo montar mi negocio.»

feedback.es: A blessing in disguise es fijo: el bien llega «disfrazado» de mal, y disguise no se sustituye por otra palabra.

origin.text: I lost my job in March, and I was terrified. Yet it turned out to be a blessing in ___, because it made me start the business that I had always dreamed of.

prompt.es: Cuenta tu lunes caótico con cuatro modismos y explica dos de ellos.

answer.text: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday. I woke up under the weather, which means that I felt a bit ill, but I went to work anyway. First my bus broke down, and then my phone died; that was the last straw, in other words, I could not take any more. I ran to the office and arrived in the nick of time, and my boss did not hit the roof, although he was not happy. Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so my bad day turned into a blessing in disguise, and I went home early to rest. My sister laughed so much when she heard the story that she promised to cook dinner for the whole family. In hindsight, it was a funny day, and I hope that next Monday will be a piece of cake.
accepted: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday. I woke up under the weather, which means that I felt a bit ill, but I went to work anyway. First my bus broke down, and then my phone died; that was the last straw, in other words, I could not take any more. I ran to the office and arrived in the nick of time, and my boss did not hit the roof, although he was not happy. Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so my bad day turned into a blessing in disguise, and I went home early to rest. My sister laughed so much when she heard the story that she promised to cook dinner for the whole family. In hindsight, it was a funny day, and I hope that next Monday will be a piece of cake.

Yesterday was a chaotic day, and I want to tell you an anecdote. In the morning I was on cloud nine because I got good news, but then my phone died and my bus broke down. That was the last straw, which means I could not take any more. Luckily, a friend drove me, and I reached the class in the nick of time. The exam was a piece of cake, so the bad morning turned out to be a blessing in disguise, in other words, a bad start with a happy ending. Later my brother spilled the beans about a surprise party, and the evening was fun. In hindsight, I would not change anything, because a chaotic day makes the best anecdote for friends.

feedback.es: La anécdota sigue una secuencia, integra cuatro modismos de distintos tipos y explica al menos dos con which means o in other words.

origin.text: Escribe una anécdota de un día caótico (unas 130 palabras, mínimo 110). Usa cuatro modismos de la unidad: al menos uno de emociones o dinero, uno de reacciones o personas y uno de los nuevos (the last straw, a blessing in disguise, in the nick of time). Explica dos de ellos con which means o in other words, como para alguien que no los conoce.

prompt.es: ¿Qué fue lo que más molestó a la autora de este correo?

choices.text: The delay itself, which ruined her plans.
That she could not read during the day.

feedback.es: Dice que la gota que colmó el vaso no fue el retraso sino la falta de explicación; el retraso incluso le dio tiempo para leer.

origin.text: Hi Sam, about Friday: honestly, the last straw for me was not the delay but the lack of any explanation. Still, the day was a blessing in disguise, because I finally had time to read. Next time, to cut a long story short, just call me.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por suerte, el último autobús llegó justo a tiempo.»

answer.text: Luckily, the last bus arrived in the nick of time

feedback.es: Luckily abre la frase con una coma y in the nick of time se mantiene entero al final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué deja entender la hablante sobre su abuelo.

choices.text: That he never believed in his own saying.
That he opened the bakery before the harvest.
That his saying turned out to be right.

feedback.es: La mala cosecha llevó a vender la tierra y abrir una panadería próspera: la hablante reconoce que el dicho de su abuelo tenía razón.

origin.audio: My grandfather used to say that a bad harvest could be a blessing in disguise. When I was younger I thought that he was joking, but last year I understood. Our harvest failed, so we sold the land, and with the money we opened a small bakery that feeds half the village today.
